title: forEach and map
objective: Use forEach to run code once per array element, and map to build a new transformed array.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Original Code Forge chapter covering idiomatic array methods beyond the book's core coverage. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Array.prototype.forEach() runs a callback function once for every element in an array, passing the current element as an argument. It's a direct replacement for a for loop when you just need to visit each item and don't need a break or continue — but forEach() itself returns undefined, so it's for side effects like console.log(), not for building something new.

Array.prototype.map() looks similar but does something different: it runs a callback once per element too, but collects whatever the callback returns into a brand-new array, the same length as the original. The original array is never changed — map() always returns a new one.

The easiest way to tell them apart: if you want to DO something with each item (print it, log it), reach for forEach(). If you want a NEW array built out of each item (doubled, uppercased, reshaped), reach for map().
explanation.rule: forEach() runs a callback per element and returns undefined; map() runs a callback per element and returns a new array of the results.

examples.title: Visiting Each Item with forEach
examples.note: forEach() calls the arrow function once per item; nothing is returned or collected.

examples.title: Building a New Array with map
examples.note: map() returns a brand-new array of the same length, one transformed value per original item. prices itself is untouched.

checks.question: const nums = [1, 2, 3]; const result = nums.map(n => n * 2); what is result?

feedback.correct: Correct — map() returns a new array of the callback's return values, one per element.
feedback.incorrect: map() collects each callback return value into a new array — here, every number doubled.

assignment.title: Double Trouble
assignment.brief: Write doubleAll(numbers) that returns a new array with every number doubled, using map (not a loop).
requirements: Return the new array without modifying the original.

hints: map() takes a callback and returns a new array — you don't need a loop or push().
Each element n should become n * 2 in the new array.
Return the result of calling numbers.map(...) directly.
